about_blocks.text: Dunham House: English-language residential rehab in the Eastern Townships
about_blocks.html: Dunham House: English-language residential rehab in the Eastern Townships

about_blocks.text: Dunham House is a residential addiction treatment centre on an 85-acre property at 1964 Chemin Scottsmore in Dunham, Quebec, near the line with West Brome. It treats adults for alcohol and drug addiction and specializes in people who also have a mental health condition. All of its programs run in English, which the centre says makes it the only one of its kind in Quebec.

It treats adults for alcohol and drug addiction and specializes in people who also have a mental health condition. about_blocks.text: The centre is a registered Canadian charity and non-profit. It was founded by Daniel Colson after a family member struggled to get through treatment in a language that was not their own. It has room for up to 38 residents, and the centre says about 800 people have been treated there.

about_blocks.text: There are three residential programs. The 30-day Foundations of Change program is for people who cannot be away from work or family for long, and it continues afterwards with outpatient aftercare in Montreal. The 90-day program goes further into emotional regulation and trauma. The 6-month program moves through stabilization, awareness and an exit plan that covers housing, work and community resources. All three follow a structured schedule six days a week with weekly counselling.

about_blocks.text: Therapy is built on CBT, DBT, motivational interviewing and relapse prevention, inside a therapeutic community. Residents also take part in equine-assisted learning at a neighbouring horse farm, group music therapy with an accredited music therapist, pottery, and horticultural therapy in a 7,000 sq. ft. vegetable garden and greenhouse. A psychiatric nurse assesses each resident, and an on-site general practitioner can refer people to a consulting psychiatrist.

about_blocks.text: Dunham House does not offer detox, and it does not admit people on methadone. The 6-month program is subsidized for people who qualify for Quebec social assistance, while the shorter programs are private pay, with financing through iFinance Medicard. After residential care, people can continue at the outpatient office in Montreal's Queen Elizabeth Health Complex, with a 12-week program, counselling, a family program, peer mentors and an alumni community.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Dunham House

answer_blocks.text: Dunham House treats addiction to alcohol and drugs, and it specializes in people who also live with a mental health condition (dual diagnosis). Addiction is the main focus. When someone needs more mental health care, the on-site psychiatric nurse and general practitioner can refer them to the consulting psychiatrist or to the centre's network of mental health partners.

faqs.question: Are the programs offered in English?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Dunham House runs all of its programs in English and describes itself as the only English-language centre in Quebec that specializes in dual diagnosis. Residents need to be able to read and understand English.
answer_blocks.html: Yes. Dunham House runs all of its programs in English and describes itself as the only English-language centre in Quebec that specializes in dual diagnosis. Residents need to be able to read and understand English.

faqs.question: How long are the residential programs?

answer_blocks.text: There are three residential programs: 30 days, 90 days and 6 months. The 6-month program moves through three phases (stabilization, awareness and an exit plan). The right length is decided during the first assessment, based on your situation.

faqs.question: How much does Dunham House cost, and is it covered?

answer_blocks.text: The centre does not publish a price list and asks you to call admissions, because cost depends on the program and length of stay. The 6-month program is subsidized for people who qualify for Quebec social assistance. The 30-day and 90-day programs are private pay, by cheque, credit card or EFT, and financing is available through iFinance Medicard.

faqs.question: Where is Dunham House and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: The residential campus is at 1964 Chemin Scottsmore in Dunham, in the Brome-Missisquoi part of the Eastern Townships (Cantons-de-l'Est). The centre puts the drive from Montreal at about an hour and a half, mostly along Autoroute 10. Cowansville is about 10 minutes away and Granby about half an hour.

faqs.question: Does Dunham House have services in Montreal?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Its outpatient office is in the Queen Elizabeth Health Complex at 2100 Marlowe Avenue, Suite 347, in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It runs a 12-week outpatient program, individual counselling (in person or remote), the family program and peer support for people leaving residential care.

faqs.question: Can family visit, and is there help for families?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Family members, partners and children can visit on weekends, and staff organize the visits. Dunham House also runs a six-week family program, online or in person in Montreal, on understanding addiction, communication and boundaries.

answer_blocks.text: Admission starts with the online form or a call to 450-263-3434 (option 1). A staff member then calls you back, and the centre says the process usually takes 2 to 4 days, although the waitlist can vary.

faqs.question: Can I bring my phone, and will I share a room?

answer_blocks.text: You can bring a phone, but cell phones, computers and tablets are not used during treatment except in an emergency. The centre has computers and phones on site for contacting family or handling work. Bedrooms hold a maximum of two people.
